mapping.original_g6_candidate: PRAGMA main.data_version used as a hard verdict for any different-connection commit during one long-lived store connection
mapping.executable_counterevidence: PR746/current G6 review demonstrated a legitimate WP103 write in the same UnifiedDB changes data_version while WP206-owned checkpoint state is unchanged; unconditional failure is therefore database-wide false positive behavior.
mapping.thin_current_solution: Keep path/device/inode as hard file identity. Use connection-local data_version only as a dirty/revalidation hint. When it changes, compute a deterministic witness over WP206-owned sqlite_schema objects plus ordered checkpoint rows. If the owned witness is unchanged, accept unrelated UnifiedDB activity and advance the local observation baseline. If the owned witness changed unexpectedly, fail closed.
mapping.why_no_revision_trigger_subsystem: Exact-current WP206 owns one bounded table and PR742 already contains an in-memory owned-surface witness repair. Adding persistent revision tables/triggers would add mutable state and schema surface without increasing current discriminator value.
mapping.authority_boundary: The owned-surface witness is a local integrity/revalidation measurement only. It is not a second canonical state store, not cross-reopen UnifiedDB authority, and not runtime/product acceptance.

external_source_alignment: SQLite data_version is connection-local and database-wide with respect to commits by other connections, matching the false-positive mechanism.
A selective SQL query over sqlite_schema and WP206-owned rows is compatible with SQLite's normal transactional snapshot semantics and avoids connection-local update-hook/session limitations.

A trigger-based persistent revision counter would require additional threat assumptions because triggers can be disabled per writer connection; therefore it is not preferred for this exact current F2 boundary.
required_acceptance_matrix: unrelated legitimate subsystem commit changes data_version but leaves owned witness stable -> continue and rebaseline
external mutation of a WP206 checkpoint row -> owned witness changes -> fail closed
external WP206 schema change -> owned witness changes -> fail closed
canonical same-connection WP206 write/recovery -> refresh owned witness and remain usable
DELETE and WAL journal modes preserve the same decision law
double-read/race capture must not admit a torn owned witness while an external commit overlaps revalidation
all higher target-runtime/effect/training/whole-system credits remain zero at repository-CI scope
residual_counterhypotheses: A foreign writer can mutate and restore WP206-owned bytes between observations; a final-state witness will not preserve that transient causal history. If detecting any historical foreign write is required, a stronger append-only/write-authority mechanism is needed.
Large future WP206 tables could make full owned-row hashing too expensive; only measured growth would justify a persistent incremental witness later.
Raw filesystem/WAL tamper is outside this SQL-level witness and remains a separate boundary.
architecture_delta: NO_NEW_BRANCH. External research independently converges on the active PR742 owned-surface witness repair. The useful delta is to preserve the two-stage dirty-hint/selective-witness contract and its counterevidence-driven tests, not to add a second revision subsystem.
next_exact_action: Trigger-4 owner should finish executable CI binding and terminal reconciliation for PR742 only after the owned-surface matrix and predecessor regressions execute at the claimed repository-component scope. Trigger-6 should consume that outcome rather than duplicate G6 mutation.
